title: Set 183

sentences.ko: 잘하고 있었거든. 근데 주말에 부모님 댁에 갔는데 엄마가 자꾸 내 접시에 음식을 더 얹어 주시는 거야. 엄마한테는 안 먹는다고 하기가 좀 힘들잖아. 그래서 뭐, 거의 원점으로 돌아왔어.
sentences.text: I was doing so well, but then we went to my parents' place for the weekend, and my mom kept putting more food on my plate, and you can't really say no to her, so yeah, I'm pretty much back where I started.

alts.text: Man, I was crushing it, then we spent the weekend at my parents' and my mom just kept piling food on my plate. You can't say no to her, so yeah, I'm basically back to square one.
I had been making good progress, but we spent the weekend at my parents' home, and my mother continued to serve me more food. It is difficult to refuse her, so I am essentially back where I began.

sentences.note: **back where I started** 는 처음 시작했던 자리로 돌아왔다는 뜻이에요. 캐주얼하게는 **back to square one** 이라고도 해요. **you can't really say no to her** 는 그 사람한테는 거절하기가 어렵다는 말이에요.

sentences.ko: 이사하는 거 정말 도와주고 싶은데, 지난달에 허리를 다쳐서 아직 괜찮지가 않아. 그래서 상자 나르는 건 안 하는 게 좋을 것 같아. 대신 이사 끝나고 들러서 짐 푸는 건 도와줄 수 있는데, 어때?
sentences.text: I'd really like to help you move, but I hurt my back last month and it's still not right, so I don't think I should be carrying boxes. I could come by after and help you unpack, though?

alts.text: Wish I could help you move, but I messed up my back last month and it's still not great, so I probably shouldn't lift boxes. I can swing by after and help unpack though?

I would very much like to help you move, but I injured my back last month and it has not fully recovered, so I do not believe I should carry boxes. Would it be helpful if I came by afterward to help you unpack?

sentences.note: **come by** 는 잠깐 들르다라는 뜻이고, 캐주얼하게는 **swing by** 라고 해요. **unpack** 은 짐을 풀다예요. 문장 끝의 **though** 는 그 대신 이건 어때 하는 느낌을 줘요.

sentences.ko: 작동은 잘 돼. 그냥 미리 솔직하게 말하는 건데, 배터리가 예전만큼 오래 안 가서 아마 거의 항상 충전기를 꽂아 두고 써야 할 거야. 그래서 50달러만 받는 거야.
sentences.text: It works fine, I just want to be upfront that the battery doesn't last like it used to, so you'll probably have to keep it plugged in most of the time. That's why I'm only asking fifty for it.

alts.text: Totally works, just so you know, the battery's not what it used to be, so you'll probably have to keep it plugged in most of the time. That's why I'm only asking fifty.

It functions properly, but I should let you know that the battery does not last as long as it once did, so you will likely need to keep it plugged in most of the time. That is why I am only asking fifty dollars for it.

sentences.note: **be upfront** 는 숨기지 않고 미리 솔직하게 말하다라는 뜻이에요. **doesn't last like it used to** 는 예전만큼 오래 가지 않는다는 말로, 물건이 낡았을 때 자주 써요.
sentences.situation: 중고로 물건 팔면서 상태 솔직히 말하기

sentences.ko: 내가 왜 판매원 말에 넘어가서 더 큰 TV를 샀나 몰라. 매장에서는 진짜 좋아 보였는데 우리 거실에 놓으니까 너무 커. 게다가 상자를 벌써 버려서 반품도 못 해.
sentences.text: I don't know why I let the sales guy talk me into the bigger TV. It looked great in the store, but in our living room it's just way too much, and I can't even return it because I already threw out the box.

alts.text: Ugh, why'd I let the sales guy talk me into the bigger TV? Looked great in the store, but in our living room it's way too much, and I can't even return it cause I already tossed the box.

I am not sure why I allowed the salesperson to persuade me to buy the larger television. It looked excellent in the store, but it is far too large for our living room, and I cannot return it because I have already discarded the box.

sentences.note: **talk me into** 는 누가 말로 설득해서 내가 뭔가를 하게 만들었다는 뜻이에요. **way too much** 는 너무 과하다, 지나치다는 말이에요. **threw out** 은 버렸다예요.

sentences.ko: 솔직히 별일 없었어. 토요일에 친구 생일 모임에 가기로 했는데 너무 피곤해서 안 갔거든. 그러고 나니까 좀 미안해서, 결국 일요일에 대신 그 친구한테 점심을 사 줬어.
sentences.text: Not much, honestly. I was supposed to go to my friend's birthday thing on Saturday, but I was so tired I bailed, and then I felt kind of bad about it, so I ended up taking her out for lunch on Sunday instead.

alts.text: Eh, not a lot. I was gonna go to my friend's birthday thing Saturday but I was wiped so I bailed, then felt kinda bad, so I took her out to lunch Sunday instead.

Not a great deal, to be honest. I had planned to attend my friend's birthday celebration on Saturday, but I was too tired and did not go. I felt somewhat guilty about it, so I took her out to lunch on Sunday instead.

sentences.note: **bailed** 는 하기로 한 약속에 막판에 빠졌다는 뜻의 구어예요. **ended up** 은 결국 ~하게 됐다, **taking her out for lunch** 는 그 사람을 데리고 나가 점심을 사 주는 거예요.

reviewed: 3번 casual 의 prob 는 문자로 쓰는 줄임말이라 말할 때는 probably 로 고침
